eval_feedback.overall: No assertion captures this difference: A uses AVX-512 and FMA and warns that results differ between Westmere and newer boxes. B deliberately leaves out FMA and AVX-512, so every CPU in the fleet returns bit-identical results, and it argues that AVX-512 is not worth it at n of a few thousand. The 'AVX2 or AVX-512' wording of 03 passes both, and nothing checks whether a response deals with results differing across machines, which matters for a library shipped to a mixed fleet. No check executes an AVX-512 path, because Rosetta stops at AVX2. A broken AVX-512 kernel would therefore pass every assertion, and A's 04 is graded on code that nobody has run. From reading it, A's kernel looks correct: a masked tail load ending at a[n-1], and 8 accumulators.
